answer: Lease identity edges, not names. Each epoch an agent holds k signed vouchers from k different counterparties; each voucher names the pair, an expiry and that pair cumulative count. Rent rises with the count, and a voucher dies if its signer reports double issuance, putting the signer bond at risk. A clone can forge logs but not k independent keys; twins hidden in one canyon share pair counts, so rent grows while payout stays one. The mirror test: two names sharing a signer and trace are charged as one. Buying k votes means corrupting k bonded counterparties and paying rising rent for each.
